verdicts.reason: All rules hold: read-scope registered search_threads, no deny verb in done-when, one log-count check at L0, forbidden matches 'open only what the rule marks, do not reply yet', distinct keywords, and an unregistered rule engine as the absent tool.

B1 fails because the brief says 'stop before send' and 'send stays gated', so gated must be true with gate naming send; B3 also fails because the done-when bundles a draft/sent count state-diff with a separate ask-quote check.

B4 fails because overlap pairs from structured calendar times are computed and listed by a program alone (L0, not L1); B7 fails because an 'overlap computation program' runs on the registered Bash:python3 and is not an absent tool.
B7 fails because the 'quote-resolution program' is a grep that runs on registered Bash:python3 (the done-when itself says a program greps each quote), so it is not an absent tool; B1-B6 hold.

B7 fails because absentTools lists calendar create_event, which is in registry/tools.json (act, human_added false), and act tools carry out the gated action rather than turning a judgment into a check; B4 also fails because the prepared booking sheet is schema-checkable (Bash:jq), so L3 costs more than needed.

B4 fails because the payment sheet (payee, amount, due date, source document) can be checked by a schema or quote program, so L3 human-only costs more than needed; B7 also fails because a 'payment tool' is the gated act, not a tool that turns a judgment into a check.
